adjustment_reviews.adjustment: Card 209 stand-down 2 (cycle 2, ctx-2): the seat that starts any wait over 20 min (the full suite included) writes its own in-flight line with the start taken from the clock at launch and cap = start + 25 min; the facilitator never writes a start or cap on a seat's behalf.
adjustment_reviews.issue: The cap for the 209 criterion 2 green came from the facilitator's estimate of a suite start (14:50 against the real 14:36:50), so the zero cap moves was partly luck.
adjustment_reviews.evidence: Metric (own-timestamp share, 209 criterion 2: 0 of 1): on the 208 criterion 1 green the developer wrote its own line (b3c246b, 18:20 UTC, cap 18:45 = start + 25) and the suite ran from 18:20 (1162.263 s, 356 tests OK, 1 skip, from the e81ed21 body); green e81ed21 at 18:40:12 UTC, inside the cap; cap moves 0 (209 criterion 1: 2). So 1 of 1 for the green suite wait. Not applied to the other waits: the QA line (30cf8a2, 17:59 UTC, 'started about 17:54', cap 18:20) and the unit-layer cap 18:41 (023e582) were written by the facilitator from estimates, and the seat's own line carries the minute only, with no statement that it came from date -u. Counter-metrics: red to green 30 min (83714f1 18:10:19Z to e81ed21 18:40:12Z) against 21 and 62, with three unit layers instead of two so not comparable; no wait held past its cap.
adjustment_reviews.side_effects: Good: the green wait was bounded by a number the seat owns and no cap moved. Bad: the suite is now 19.4 min (356 tests) against 17.2, so start + 25 leaves 5.6 min of margin; the rule was read as covering only the suite, so the QA and unit-layer waits (16 and 30 min) still ran on facilitator caps.
adjustment_reviews.verdict: keep, with the tune folded into this stand-down's adjustment (the same own-line rule at every seat start, with the clock source stated).

adjustment_reviews.adjustment: D158 facilitator pre-window checklist (card 209 retro pick; seats, caps, working directory, line endings), first card under it.
adjustment_reviews.issue: Window and wait drift on 209: a verification run that executed another repository's suite (15:57 UTC), caps from estimates, and line-ending churn in seat commits.
adjustment_reviews.evidence: Before (209): wrong-directory verification run, two cap moves on the criterion 1 green, whole-file CRLF rewrite in 44112b4 (1181 raw lines for 123 net). After (208, git): four checklists committed before their windows (4b51ec6, b138c0e, 3a4f777 for two), each listing seats, working directory with a hash, and probes; all four windows decided with every seat polled. Criterion 1 raw and --ignore-cr-at-eol stats are identical on all four commits (158, 171, 4 and 49 changed lines), so no churn. But the line-endings line reads 'no seat edits in a window; n/a' in all four blocks, so that clause was never exercised and the churn-free result is not credited to it; the Caps line is 'no wait over 20 minutes' with no source, so the 'cap names its source' clause is not met by the checklist; no verification run happened in a window, so its working-directory clause is untested. No checklist exists for the non-window seat waits (QA red, developer green), where the 209 problems lived.
adjustment_reviews.side_effects: Good: seats and working directory are readable from the records for every window. Bad: the four blocks are near copies (a write cost with little new information), and they cover only windows, so the checklist missed the seat waits it was written for.
adjustment_reviews.verdict: tune: keep the window blocks; add cap source, working directory with repository top level and the line-ending instruction (from git ls-files --eol) to the in-flight line of every seat start, which this stand-down's adjustment does.
